text: Every DBA in this catalog has had to answer the same question: if this database disappears right now, how do I get it back? Neo4j answers it with neo4j-admin database backup and restore — and the real capability you get depends heavily on which edition you're running.

The simplest, most universal approach works in every edition, including Community: stop the database, copy its data directory, start it back up. Conceptually identical to stopping SQL Server and copying the .mdf and .ldf files directly — reliable, but completely unavailable while the business needs the database up.

neo4j-admin database backup takes a consistent backup of a running database with no downtime — but this is where the licensing line actually falls. Online, non-disruptive backup is an Enterprise Edition feature. Community Edition can only do the stop-copy-start pattern.

Restore targets a stopped instance, the same way a SQL Server restore does. The overwrite-destination flag is the explicit, deliberate safeguard against silently clobbering a live database by accident — the same instinct as WITH REPLACE on a SQL Server RESTORE DATABASE statement.

Enterprise Edition also supports incremental backups after an initial full backup, the same efficiency argument behind SQL Server's differentials. Next up: causal clustering and high availability in Neo4j.
